title: APODICTIC: predicting the contract
alt: Flowchart. Your manuscript goes in, and APODICTIC predicts its contract from the text alone: genre, reader promise and controlling idea. That prediction is compared with the contract you intended. Where they match, the book is measured against its contract in genre-calibrated passes. Where they differ, the mismatch is the signal that the text is not communicating what you think. Both lead to the editorial letter, which names classes of solution and never rewrites your prose.

steps.caption: APODICTIC reads your manuscript before it hears your plans.
From the text alone it predicts the contract: genre, the promise to readers, and the controlling idea.
Then it sets that prediction beside the contract you meant to write.
Where they match, the book is measured against its own contract. A slow opening is fine in literary fiction and a defect in a thriller.
Where they differ, that mismatch is the diagnosis: the text is not communicating what you think it is.
Both feed the editorial letter, which names classes of solution and never rewrites your prose. Argument pieces get the same check against claim, audience, burden and stakes.
